tools.name: analyze
tools.description: Full project analysis. Use on first run or after major structural changes (new files, renames, deleted code). An optional extractor executable is named by CHISEL_EXTRACTOR or .chisel/extensions.toml. Chisel does not link that program. Scans source files, extracts code units, discovers tests, parses git history, builds test-to-code edges. For incremental changes, use 'update' instead. Large repos: run `chisel analyze --force` in a terminal (not only via MCP) so long runs are not mistaken for a hung tool. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

force.description: Force re-analysis of all files even if unchanged.

shard.description: Optional shard key to scope analysis to one shard snapshot (sharded monorepos via CHISEL_SHARDS or .chisel/shards.toml). Omit to rely on automatic path-based routing.

tools.name: impact
tools.description: Get impacted tests for specific changed files/functions. Use when you know exactly which files changed. For auto-detection from git diff, use 'diff_impact' instead. Cross-shard edges from the parent snapshot are included. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

functions.description: Optional list of changed function names.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: suggest_tests
tools.description: Suggest tests to run for a file, ranked by relevance. Includes cross-shard edges. flakiness_trend is set when dated results span two weeks. Combines direct test edges, git co-change, and static import-graph reachability (e.g. facade tests covering inner modules). Each item includes a source: direct | co_change | import_graph | static_require | hybrid | fallback | working_tree. Confidence ranking (highest first): hybrid > direct > import_graph > co_change > static_require > working_tree > fallback. hybrid means BOTH the snapshot test edges AND a static scan of test-file imports agree on the same test — these are the safest to trust and typically score ~0.5 (vs ~0.4 for direct alone or ~0.16 for import_graph alone). With working_tree=true, also indexes untracked test files and git-untracked source paths for resolution. Returns empty for untracked/new files unless fallback_to_all or working_tree is set. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

file_path.description: Path to the file to suggest tests for. Trust ranking: hybrid > direct > import_graph > co_change > static_require > working_tree > fallback. When both hybrid and direct items appear for the same test, hybrid wins — it has corroboration from both the snapshot edge graph and a static import scan.

fallback_to_all.description: If true and no test edges exist for the file, return all known test files ranked by name similarity instead of empty. Useful for new/untracked files that have no analysis data yet.

working_tree.description: If true, also scan untracked (uncommitted) files on disk and use stem-matching to find relevant tests when the file has no snapshot edges. useful during active development before files are committed.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: churn
tools.description: Get change frequency for a file or specific function. High churn = frequently modified = higher risk. Use to understand why a file has a high risk score.

unit_name.description: Optional name of a specific code unit.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: ownership
tools.description: Get original authors of a file via git blame. Returns role='original_author'. For active maintainers/reviewers, use 'who_reviews' instead.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: coupling
tools.description: Get files that frequently change together (co-change coupling) or share static import edges (structural coupling). Returns co_change_partners, import_partners, and numeric import_coupling / effective_coupling scores. Import coupling is reliable in all projects; co-change coupling requires multi-author commit history with many small commits — solo projects or bulk-commit workflows will show 0.0 co-change (use import_partners instead). Pass working_tree=true for untracked files (computes import_partners from on-disk static analysis even before analyze). Threshold scales with project maturity (see 'stats' for current value). Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: risk_map
tools.description: Risk scores for all files combining churn, coupling (git co-change and/or static import graph), coverage gaps, author concentration, and test instability (failure rate + duration variance). flakiness_trend is included when dated results span two weeks. It does not change risk weights. Cross-shard coverage is included. Returns {files: [...], _meta: {effective_components, uniform_components, uniform_risk_groups, max_identical_risk_files, warnings, reweighted, effective_weights, coverage_gap_mode, coupling_threshold, total_test_edges, total_test_results}}. Check _meta.uniform_components and _meta.uniform_risk_groups to identify metrics or files with no differentiating signal (e.g. 5+ files sharing identical 0.75 risk). Use as first step to prioritize which files need attention. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

directory.description: Optional subdirectory to scope the risk map.

exclude_tests.description: Exclude test files (default: true). Test files always score coverage_gap=1.0, adding noise.

proximity_adjustment.description: If true, slightly reduce coverage_gap for files a few import hops from code covered by tests (see _meta.coverage_gap_mode).

coverage_mode.description: 'line' (default) weights by line count so large untested units have proportionally higher coverage_gap; 'unit' weights each code unit equally.

working_tree.description: If true, include untracked code files in the risk map so newly created files are visible.

auto_update.description: If true, attempt an incremental update before scoring so recent changes are reflected.

exclude_new_file_boost.description: If true, suppress the 0.5 new-file boost so long-term risk rankings are not skewed toward recently touched files.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: stale_tests
tools.description: Find tests whose source targets have changed since last analysis. Uses analyzed snapshot test edges only (not a working-tree scan of untracked tests). Use to identify tests that may need updating.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Commit history for a specific file. Use for understanding change patterns or finding when a bug was introduced.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: who_reviews
tools.description: Suggest reviewers based on recent commit activity. Returns role='suggested_reviewer' — active maintainers, not original authors. For original authors, use 'ownership' instead.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: record_result
tools.description: Record a test pass/fail outcome with recorded_at. Feeds into suggest_tests (failure rate and flakiness_trend) and risk_map (test instability). Pytest ids with :: are stored with a single colon. Call this after every test run so Chisel can boost flaky tests and compute accurate risk scores over time.

tools.name: diff_impact
tools.description: Use after editing code to find which tests to run. Auto-detects changed files/functions from git diff and includes untracked code files. On feature branches diffs against main; on main diffs HEAD. Untracked files with no snapshot edges fall back to stem-matching (source=working_tree). With working_tree=true, performs full static import scanning for untracked files (matching suggest_tests behavior) to find tests that import new files by path. Returns diagnostic when no changes detected. If git fails (wrong cwd, not a repo), returns status=git_error with error (not_a_git_repo or git_command_failed), cwd, message, and project_dir — never silent empty lists. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

ref.description: Git ref to diff against (default: HEAD for unstaged changes).

working_tree.description: If true, perform full static import scanning for untracked files instead of only stem-match fallback. Recommended during active development before files are committed.

auto_update.description: If true, attempt an incremental update when changed files are missing from the snapshot before returning results.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: update
tools.description: Incremental re-analysis — only changed files and new commits. Use instead of full 'analyze' after small edits. For large repos or slow MCP clients, prefer `chisel update` / `chisel analyze` in a terminal so the run cannot time out in silence.

shard.description: Optional shard key to scope the update to one shard snapshot. Omit to rely on automatic path-based routing.

tools.name: stats
tools.description: Snapshot counts plus coupling threshold. When shards are configured, cross_shard_test_edges is a count. stats does not return the full result history. Use to verify analysis state or diagnose empty results from other tools. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

tools.name: optimize_storage
tools.description: Rewrite the .chisel/store snapshot to drop expired lock rows. Use periodically on a long-lived project. This does not open chisel.db or run SQLite. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: test_gaps
tools.description: Find code units with no test coverage, sorted by churn risk. Use to decide which tests to write first. Excludes test files by default. If the snapshot has no test edges but a JS/TS relative import or Go import resolves to the source path, that file is treated as covered. With working_tree=true, untracked tests/paths are included in that scan. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

directory.description: Scope to a directory (file_path takes precedence).

exclude_tests.description: Exclude units from test files (default: true).

working_tree.description: If true, also scan untracked (uncommitted) files from disk and include their code units as gaps with churn=0. useful for identifying coverage gaps in files that haven't been committed yet.

auto_update.description: If true, attempt an incremental update before querying so recent changes are reflected.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: triage
tools.description: Combined risk + test gaps + stale tests for top-N files. Use as the first reconnaissance step before audits or refactors. Single call replaces risk_map + test_gaps + stale_tests. Zero crate dependencies. The snapshot is .chisel/store. Parsing is heuristic and git is a subprocess. Confirm safety-critical paths in CI.

directory.description: Optional subdirectory to scope the triage.

top_n.description: Number of top-risk files to include (default: 10).

exclude_tests.description: Exclude test files from risk ranking (default: true).

working_tree.description: If true, forward working_tree to risk_map and test_gaps so uncommitted files are included.

auto_update.description: If true, attempt an incremental update before triaging so recent changes are reflected.

exclude_new_file_boost.description: If true, suppress the 0.5 new-file boost in the risk portion of triage so rankings are more stable over time.

tools.name: start_job
tools.description: Run full analyze or incremental update in a background thread; poll job_status with the returned job_id. Use when MCP clients would time out on long analyze/update (zero crate dependencies; one background thread in this process).

shard.description: Optional shard key to scope the job to one shard snapshot. Omit to rely on automatic path-based routing.

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Poll a job started with start_job. Returns status running | completed | failed | not_found; completed includes result dict; failed includes error.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Request cooperative cancellation of a running background job started with start_job. Returns ok (cancellation requested), error (job already completed/failed), or not_found. Poll job_status to confirm the job stopped.

tools.name: acquire_file_lock
tools.description: Acquire an advisory lock on a file before editing. Other agents checking this file will see you hold the lock. Use ttl to set how long the lock persists before auto-expiry (default 300s).

file_path.description: File path to lock (normalized relative path).

agent_id.description: Unique identifier for the requesting agent.

tools.name: release_file_lock
tools.description: Release an advisory lock held by this agent. Returns false if the lock is not held by this agent.

tools.name: refresh_file_lock
tools.description: Extend the TTL of a lock held by this agent. Call periodically while actively editing a locked file.

tools.name: check_file_lock
tools.description: Check if a file is currently locked. Returns lock holder info or null if the file is not locked.

tools.name: check_locks
tools.description: Batch-check lock status for multiple files at once. Use before starting work to check for collisions.

file_paths.description: List of file paths to check.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.

tools.name: list_file_locks
tools.description: List all active file locks, optionally filtered by agent. Use to audit what other agents are working on.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.
